title: Too many dogs still lack safe placement
summary: Dogs continue entering a local animal-welfare system constrained by shelter space, veterinary capacity, foster and rescue placement, and access to spay/neuter services.
what_we_are_seeing: Stray and abandoned dogs continue to be reported across Stockton.
City records say stray animal intakes regularly exceed shelter capacity.
The local response includes street outreach, sheltering, veterinary treatment, foster and adoption, rescue transfers, and spay/neuter work.
contributing_factors: Animal overpopulation and unplanned litters
Limited spay and neuter capacity
Shelter and placement capacity pressure
Limited access to affordable and timely veterinary care
Abandonment and stray intake
Insufficient foster, rescue, and permanent placement

title: People with pets still face barriers to safe shelter
summary: Pet ownership remains a documented barrier to some shelter and housing options, even as Stockton adds low-barrier capacity designed to keep people with their companion animals.
what_we_are_seeing: San Joaquin County's 2024 survey found 34% of unhoused respondents had a pet, and 45% of pet-owning respondents had two or more pets.
The 2026 homelessness count added a specific question to measure whether pets are preventing people from entering shelter.
St. Mary's Pathways now provides low-barrier shelter options designed to accommodate people with pets, partners, family, or belongings.
Stockton Streetdogs is also pursuing a Safe Grounds model intended to keep unhoused people and companion animals together while they move toward housing.
contributing_factors: Pet restrictions in some shelter and housing settings
Limited pet-inclusive shelter and transitional capacity
Multiple pets can make placement harder
Need for pet food, veterinary care, crates, and other support infrastructure
Fear of separation from companion animals

title: Food distribution capacity isn't keeping up with need
summary: Large food donations and strong community demand are colliding with limited cold storage, refrigerated transport, and the logistics needed to move food quickly across Stockton and San Joaquin County.
what_we_are_seeing: A roughly three-semitruck frozen-food donation exceeded Bread of Life's two existing freezers in August 2026.
Bread of Life relied on local partners for refrigerated transportation and temporary cold storage so the donation could still reach residents.
Bread of Life currently reports distributing through more than 33 locations and serving about 7,000 people per month.
Community Partnership for Families also provides neighborhood food distribution and fresh-food access through its Family Resource Centers.
contributing_factors: Limited cold-storage capacity
Need for refrigerated transportation and temporary overflow storage
Large multi-site distribution footprint
High household demand
Distribution labor and coordination needs

title: People leaving incarceration still face unstable reentry housing
summary: Housing, work, and basic stability have to come together after incarceration. Stockton has active reentry pathways, but stable housing remains one of the core conditions for a successful second chance.
what_we_are_seeing: Ready To Work currently combines transitional housing, paid work, case management, training, and links to permanent housing for eligible men.
Friends Outside currently provides housing and rental assistance, employment readiness, basic-needs support, and case management for people returning from incarceration.
Friends Outside identifies housing alongside education and employment as one of the three pillars of successful reentry.
The prison puppy-raising program at California Health Care Facility in Stockton provides a related pre-release pathway centered on responsibility, service, and connection.
contributing_factors: Difficulty securing stable housing after incarceration
Employment and income instability during reentry
Criminal-record barriers
Multiple needs arriving at once after release
Need for family, community, and case-management support
current_state: Stockton has active housing-and-work reentry programs, but those programs themselves continue to treat stable housing as a central condition for successful reintegration.

title: People still need low-barrier paths from homelessness to housing
summary: Stockton still faces substantial homelessness, but new low-barrier shelter and navigation capacity is creating more direct paths from the street toward stable housing.
what_we_are_seeing: St. Mary’s opened Pathways Neighborhood in June 2026, adding 268 beds of modular transitional housing with on-site supportive services.
The Pathways model is explicitly focused on low-barrier shelter, case management, wraparound services, and movement toward permanent housing.
The Zeiter Navigation Center is another major St. Mary’s housing-navigation asset in downtown Stockton.
Stockton leaders still identify homelessness as a major city challenge even as this new capacity comes online.
contributing_factors: Persistent homelessness and housing instability
Need for low-barrier shelter options
Need for case management and housing navigation
Behavioral and physical health needs
Shortage of stable and affordable permanent housing
